q: A radial drilling machine is preferred for drilling holes in a large and heavy workpiece mainly because:

options.A: It drills holes of a smaller diameter than other machines
options.B: Its spindle runs at a lower speed than that of other drilling machines
options.C: It requires no drill bit for making the holes
options.D: Its arm can swing and its drill head can travel along the arm, so that holes at different positions can be drilled without moving the workpiece

e: On a radial drilling machine the arm swings about the column and the drill head travels along the arm, so the spindle can be brought over any point of a large heavy workpiece. Holes at different positions are thus drilled without moving the workpiece.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Creep is the slow and progressive deformation of a material under a sustained load, occurring particularly at high temperatures.
2. Creep is the failure of a component under repeated fluctuating stresses.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Creep is the slow progressive deformation of a material under a sustained load, occurring particularly at high temperatures. Failure under repeated fluctuating stresses is fatigue, not creep; so only statement 1 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Ductility is the property by which a metal can be drawn out into wires without breaking.
2. Plasticity is the property by which a material undergoes permanent deformation under load without fracturing.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Ductility is the property by which a metal can be drawn out into wires without breaking, and plasticity is the property of undergoing permanent deformation under load without fracturing. Both properties are correctly defined; both statements are correct.

q: Elasticity of a material means the property by which it:

options.A: Undergoes permanent deformation without fracture
options.B: Regains its original shape and size on the removal of the load, so long as the load is within the elastic limit
options.C: Can be hammered into thin sheets without rupture
options.D: Resists indentation and scratching of its surface

e: Elasticity is the property by which a material regains its original shape and size on removal of the load, so long as the load is within its elastic limit. Beyond that limit, permanent deformation remains.

q: Work hardening (strain hardening) of a metal means:

options.A: Hardening of the surface of a metal by heating and quenching
options.B: Coating of a metal with a hard deposit of another metal
options.C: Softening of a metal by prolonged heating at a high temperature
options.D: The increase in the hardness and strength of a metal caused by plastic deformation at ordinary temperature, as in cold drawing or cold rolling

e: Work hardening or strain hardening is the increase in hardness and strength of a metal caused by plastic deformation at ordinary temperature, as in cold drawing, cold rolling or cold hammering, without any heat treatment.

q: A screw pitch gauge is used in a workshop for:

options.A: Measuring the depth of a drilled hole
options.B: Measuring the angle of a tapered workpiece
options.C: Checking the pitch of a screw thread, by matching its toothed blades against the thread
options.D: Checking the flatness of a surface

e: A screw pitch gauge has a set of toothed blades of different pitches. Matching a blade against the thread of a screw or bolt checks its pitch, the blade that fits exactly indicating the pitch.

q: A depth gauge is an instrument used in a workshop for measuring:

options.A: The angle between two faces of a component
options.B: The internal diameter of a cylinder
options.C: The pitch of a screw thread
options.D: The depth of holes, grooves and recesses

e: A depth gauge measures the depth of holes, grooves, recesses and steps, using a beam or rod that slides through a base resting on the surface. It does not measure angles, diameters or thread pitch.

q: A fitter has marked out the centre of a hole to be drilled on a component and wants the drill to start exactly at the marked point without wandering. Before drilling, he makes a small indentation at the marked centre with:

options.A: A scriber
options.B: A centre punch
options.C: A surface gauge
options.D: A divider

e: A centre punch makes a small conical indentation exactly at the marked centre of a hole to be drilled. The indentation guides the drill point at starting and prevents it from wandering off the mark.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the shaft-basis system of limits and fits, the size of the shaft is kept constant and the size of the hole is varied to obtain the different classes of fit.
2. The shaft-basis system is the system generally preferred in workshop practice, because holes are made by standard tools of fixed size.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under the shaft-basis system the shaft size is kept constant and the hole size is varied to obtain different fits, so statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the hole-basis system is the one generally preferred, because holes are made with standard tools of fixed size while shafts are easily varied.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a clearance fit, the shaft is always smaller than the hole, so that a clearance remains between the two when assembled.
2. In an interference fit, the shaft is larger than the hole, so that the parts have to be forced or shrunk together on assembly.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In a clearance fit the shaft is always smaller than the hole, leaving clearance on assembly so the parts move freely. In an interference fit the shaft is larger than the hole and the parts must be forced or shrunk together; both statements are correct.

q: In the limits and fits system, the allowance provided on a dimension means:

options.A: The difference between the maximum and minimum limits of one dimension
options.B: The extra material left on a casting for machining it to size
options.C: The wear permitted on a gauge before it is withdrawn from use
options.D: The intentional difference between the basic sizes of a mating hole and shaft, provided to secure the desired type of fit

e: Allowance in limits and fits is the intentional difference between the basic sizes of the mating hole and shaft, provided to secure the desired type of fit. It is distinct from tolerance, which is the difference between the maximum and minimum limits of one dimension.

q: A template used in the fabrication and fitting shops of a workshop is:

options.A: A gauge used for checking the pitch of screw threads
options.B: A plate or pattern of the exact profile required, used for marking out and for checking the shape of components made repeatedly
options.C: A standard drawing supplied by the headquarters office
options.D: A form on which the time booked by a worker is recorded

e: A template is a plate or pattern of the exact profile required, used for marking out components made repeatedly and for checking their shape. It ensures uniformity of repeated work in fabrication and fitting shops.

q: Steel components of a workshop are immersed in an acid bath before they are painted or coated, in order to remove scale and rust from their surface. This cleaning process is known as:

options.A: Fettling
options.B: Galvanising
options.C: Pickling
options.D: Tumbling

e: Pickling is the immersion of steel components in an acid bath to remove scale and rust from the surface before painting or coating. Fettling cleans castings, galvanising coats with zinc and tumbling cleans small parts in a rotating barrel.

q: Rewinding of an armature in the electrical shop of a workshop consists of:

options.A: Replacing the burnt-out winding of the armature with new coils, so that the motor or dynamo can work again
options.B: Turning the armature on a lathe to restore its roundness
options.C: Recharging the battery connected with the dynamo
options.D: Replacing the brushes of the machine with new ones

e: Rewinding an armature means stripping out its burnt-out or defective winding and replacing it with new coils of insulated wire, restoring the motor or dynamo to working order. It is more than replacing brushes or machining the armature.

q: A heavy rotating part of a workshop machine is found to vibrate badly when run at speed, because its mass is not evenly distributed about its axis of rotation. The vibration is corrected by:

options.A: Running the part at a lower speed permanently
options.B: Dynamic balancing of the part, by adding or removing material at the proper places so that its mass is evenly distributed about the axis
options.C: Tightening all the holding-down bolts of the machine
options.D: Lubricating the bearings of the part more frequently

e: Vibration of a heavy rotating part at speed due to uneven mass distribution is corrected by dynamic balancing - adding or removing material at the proper places so the mass is evenly distributed about the axis of rotation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Dressing a grinding wheel removes the dull grains and the metal embedded in its face and restores its cutting action.
2. Dressing and truing of a grinding wheel are one and the same operation, truing also meaning the sharpening of the wheel.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Dressing a grinding wheel removes dull grains and embedded metal from its face and restores its cutting action, so statement 1 is correct. Truing is a different operation - making the wheel run concentric and restoring its shape - so statement 2, equating the two, is wrong.

q: A divider, as used in marking out work in a fitting shop, is used for:

options.A: Punching the centres of holes to be drilled
options.B: Scribing circles and arcs on a workpiece and stepping off equal distances on it
options.C: Testing the squareness of a workpiece
options.D: Measuring the depth of a recess in a workpiece

e: A divider has two pointed legs hinged together and is used in marking out to scribe circles and arcs on a workpiece and to step off equal distances along a line, transferring dimensions from a rule.

q: A mallet used by fitters and carpenters in a workshop differs from an ordinary hammer in that the mallet:

options.A: Is driven by compressed air instead of by hand
options.B: Has a head of soft material such as wood, rawhide or plastic, so that it can strike finished or delicate surfaces without damaging them
options.C: Has two sharp cutting edges on its head
options.D: Is used only for breaking up concrete and stone

e: A mallet has a head of soft material such as wood, rawhide or plastic. It is used to strike blows on finished or delicate surfaces, chisels and assembly work without damaging the surface, unlike a steel hammer.

q: Bars and rods of raw material required in the machine shop are cut off to the lengths needed for jobs mainly on:

options.A: A centre lathe, by the parting off operation
options.B: A power hacksaw or a band saw
options.C: A milling machine
options.D: A shaping machine

e: Bars and rods are cut off to job lengths mainly on a power hacksaw or a band saw, which are designed for cutting off stock quickly and economically. Using a lathe, milling or shaping machine for routine cutting off would be wasteful.

q: Soldering, as a method of joining metal parts in a workshop, consists of:

options.A: Joining the parts with a filler metal, called solder, which melts at a relatively low temperature, the parts themselves not being melted
options.B: Fusing the edges of the parts together without any filler metal
options.C: Joining the parts by pressure while they are heated to a plastic state
options.D: Joining the parts with a filler metal which melts at a temperature above that of the parts joined

e: Soldering joins metal parts with a filler metal called solder, which melts at a relatively low temperature and wets the joint, the parts themselves not being melted. This low melting point distinguishes it from welding and brazing.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A bin card is maintained at the bin or rack in the stores depot and records only the quantities of material received, issued and in balance.
2. The stores ledger maintained in the accounts office records both the quantities and the values of receipts, issues and balances.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A bin card, kept at the bin in the depot, records only quantities received, issued and in balance. The stores ledger in the accounts office records both quantities and values of receipts, issues and balances; both statements are correct.

q: A workshop fabricated a special die for a manufacture job which has since been given up, and the die cannot be used for any other work. When a proposal to take up a fresh job is now examined, the cost already incurred on the die is treated, for the purpose of that decision, as:

options.A: A part of the material cost of the fresh job
options.B: A sunk cost, already incurred and irrecoverable, and therefore not relevant to the fresh choice
options.C: A part of the general on-cost of the workshop for the current year
options.D: A sum recoverable from the stores depot which received the die

e: The cost already incurred on a die for an abandoned job is irrecoverable and cannot be altered by any future decision. For examining a fresh job proposal it is a sunk cost and is not relevant to that choice.

q: In costing terminology, 'differential cost' means:

options.A: The cost which differs from shop to shop for the same article
options.B: The fixed cost of a shop divided by its outturn
options.C: The cost of the defective output of a process
options.D: The change in total cost that results from choosing one course of action, or one level of activity, in place of another

e: Differential cost is the change in total cost that results from choosing one course of action, or one level of activity, in place of another. Decisions between alternatives are judged on this difference in cost, together with any difference in revenue.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A railway workshop works on a no-profit-no-loss basis, its outturn being transferred to the final heads at cost, without the addition of any profit.
2. A workshop is treated as a profit centre, its efficiency being judged by the margin earned on the overhaul work done for its own railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A railway workshop works on a no-profit-no-loss basis: its outturn is transferred to the final heads at cost, with no profit added, so statement 1 is correct. It is not run as a profit centre judged by a margin on its own railway's work; statement 2 is wrong.

q: The bottleneck machine of a machine shop can be used either on an urgent job of the home railway or on a deposit job for an outside party, which would bring in a recovery. If the home railway job is taken up, the recovery forgone on the deposit job represents, in costing terms:

options.A: A sunk cost of the machine shop
options.B: A direct cost of the home railway job
options.C: The opportunity cost of using the machine on the home railway job
options.D: A part of the shop on-cost of the machine shop

e: Using the bottleneck machine on the home railway job means forgoing the recovery the deposit job would have brought in. That benefit forgone is the opportunity cost of using the machine on the home railway job.

q: The efficiency ratio used in standard costing in a workshop compares:

options.A: The budgeted overheads of a shop with its actual overheads
options.B: The standard hours earned for the actual output with the actual hours taken to produce it
options.C: The standard cost of material with the actual cost of material
options.D: The machine hours worked in a shop with the labour hours booked in it

e: The efficiency ratio in standard costing compares the standard hours earned for the actual output with the actual hours taken to produce it. A ratio below 100 percent shows more time was taken than the standard allows.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the perpetual inventory system, the stores records are posted with every receipt and issue, so that the balance in stock is known at any time, and physical verification is carried out continuously, in rotation.
2. Under this system, physical verification of stores can be dispensed with altogether, the book balances being accepted as final.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under perpetual inventory, stores records are posted with every receipt and issue so the book balance is known at any time, and physical verification is done continuously in rotation. Verification is not dispensed with - it is spread through the year - so only statement 1 is correct.

q: At a cost review, the incharge of a shop is asked to explain an increase in the general on-cost apportioned to his shop, the amount of that on-cost being fixed for the workshop as a whole. The correct position in costing terms is that:

options.A: He must make good the increase by reducing the direct labour booked on jobs
options.B: The apportioned general on-cost is a direct cost of his shop's jobs
options.C: It is a part of his controllable cost, since it appears in his shop's accounts
options.D: It is not a controllable cost at his level; he is answerable for the costs which his own decisions in the shop govern, such as usage of material and idle time

e: General on-cost apportioned to a shop is fixed for the workshop as a whole and is not governed by the shop incharge's decisions, so it is not a controllable cost at his level. He is answerable for costs his own decisions control, such as material usage and idle time in his shop.

q: Under a group technology (cellular) layout in a workshop:

options.A: All machines of one type are grouped together in one shop
options.B: The machines are arranged in a line in the sequence of operations of a single product
options.C: Machines are arranged in cells, each cell having the machines needed to complete a family of similar components
options.D: The product remains stationary and the machines are brought to it

e: Under group technology or cellular layout, machines are grouped in cells, each cell containing the different machines needed to complete a family of similar components. The family is thus processed largely within one cell, reducing movement and waiting.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a fixed-position layout, the product is moved from machine to machine as it is progressively worked upon.
2. In a fixed-position layout, the product remains at one place and the men, machines and material are brought to it, a method suited to very large and heavy products.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In a fixed-position layout the product remains at one place and men, machines and material are brought to it, suiting very large and heavy products like locomotives under erection. Statement 1, which moves the product from machine to machine, describes a process layout; only statement 2 is correct.

q: During the Periodic Overhaul of a coach, a component is found still within its wear limits, but it figures in the list of items prescribed for renewal at every overhaul. The correct course is to:

options.A: Renew the component in accordance with the prescribed list, its present serviceability notwithstanding
options.B: Retain the component and cancel the renewal, since it is still serviceable
options.C: Renew the component only if a spare happens to be available in the shop
options.D: Postpone the renewal to the next overhaul of the coach

e: Items prescribed for renewal at every Periodic Overhaul are must-change items under the overhaul schedule. They are renewed in accordance with the prescribed list even if the removed component is still within wear limits, to ensure reliability for the full run to the next overhaul.

q: In the maintenance of workshop machinery, 'MTTR' (Mean Time To Repair) indicates:

options.A: The average interval between two successive breakdowns of a machine
options.B: The total time for which machines remained idle in a year
options.C: The time for which a spare machine is kept in reserve for a shop
options.D: The average time taken to repair a machine after a breakdown and restore it to working order

e: MTTR, Mean Time To Repair, is the average time taken to repair a machine after a breakdown and restore it to working order. The average interval between successive breakdowns is a different measure, MTBF.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Cost audit is an examination of the cost accounts and costing records of a unit to verify that costs have been correctly ascertained and that the prescribed costing principles and procedures have been followed.
2. Cost audit is the statutory audit which certifies the financial statements of the railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Cost audit examines the cost accounts and costing records to verify that costs have been correctly ascertained and prescribed costing principles and procedures followed, so statement 1 is correct. It is not the statutory audit certifying the financial statements; statement 2 is wrong.

q: A control chart, as used in statistical quality control in a workshop, is:

options.A: A chart showing the duties of the inspection staff of a workshop
options.B: A chart on which the measurements of samples taken from production are plotted as the work proceeds, so that undue variation in the process is spotted and corrected in time
options.C: A chart on which the allowed times of the jobs of a shop are displayed
options.D: A register in which the articles rejected on inspection are entered

e: A control chart plots measurements of samples taken from production, as work proceeds, against control limits. Points going out of control or showing a trend reveal undue variation in the process in time for correction before much defective work is made.

q: At the periodical physical verification of machinery and plant of a workshop, a machine entered in the Plant Register is not found in the shop to which it stands recorded. The correct course is to:

options.A: Strike the item off the Plant Register at once, since it is not available
options.B: Charge the value of the machine to the jobs in hand in the shop
options.C: Investigate the discrepancy, and strike the item off the register only after the matter is enquired into and the loss is written off under competent sanction
options.D: Enter another machine of the workshop against the missing entry

e: A machine in the Plant Register not found at verification must first be investigated; it may be transferred, under repair or mis-recorded. It is struck off the register only after enquiry and after the loss, if established, is written off under competent sanction.

q: Patrol inspection in a workshop means:

options.A: Inspection of a completed lot of articles before it is despatched
options.B: Inspection of the first piece produced in a batch
options.C: Inspection of the workshop premises by the security staff on their rounds
options.D: Inspection carried out by an inspector moving round the shops during production, checking the work at the machines at intervals while it is being produced

e: Patrol inspection is carried out by an inspector moving round the shops during production and checking work at the machines at intervals while it is being produced. Defects are thus caught during manufacture rather than after a lot is completed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In method study, the existing method of doing a job is first recorded factually, with the help of charts and diagrams, before it is examined.
2. Critical examination in method study is applied to the facts so recorded, each activity being questioned as to its purpose, place, sequence, person and means.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In method study the existing method is first recorded factually with charts and diagrams, and critical examination is then applied to the recorded facts, questioning each activity as to purpose, place, sequence, person and means. Both statements correctly state the record and examine steps.

q: In motion study, a 'cyclograph' of the movements of a worker is obtained by:

options.A: Attaching a small electric light to the hand of the worker and photographing the path traced by the light as the work is done
options.B: Timing the worker with a stop watch over a number of cycles of the job
options.C: Counting the units produced by the worker in a shift
options.D: Filming the worker at normal speed for showing in training classes

e: A cyclograph is obtained by attaching a small electric light to the worker's hand and photographing, with a time exposure, the path traced by the light as the work is done. The resulting light trace shows the smoothness and economy of the movement path.

q: A motor rewound in the electrical shop of a workshop is to be returned to service. Before it is put on load, the soundness of the insulation of its windings is tested with:

options.A: An ammeter connected in the supply circuit of the motor
options.B: A megger (insulation tester), which measures the resistance of the insulation
options.C: A wattmeter measuring the power taken by the motor
options.D: A tachometer measuring the speed of the motor

e: Before a rewound motor is put on load, the insulation resistance of its windings is tested with a megger, an insulation tester that applies a high test voltage and measures resistance. A satisfactory megger reading proves the insulation is sound.

q: The commutator of a direct-current machine, attended to in the electrical shop of a workshop, is the device which:

options.A: Carries the field winding of the machine
options.B: Supports the armature shaft in its bearings
options.C: Reverses the connections of the armature winding as the armature rotates, so that the current in the external circuit remains in one direction
options.D: Blows air through the machine for its cooling

e: The commutator of a DC machine reverses the connections of the armature winding as the armature rotates. This keeps the current in the external circuit in one direction, converting the alternating current generated in the winding into direct current outside.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In blanking on a press, the piece punched out of the sheet is the required article, the sheet left behind being scrap.
2. In piercing on a press, the hole made in the sheet is what is required, and the piece punched out is scrap.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In blanking, the piece punched out of the sheet is the required article and the remaining sheet is scrap. In piercing, the hole made is what is required and the piece punched out is scrap; both statements are correct.

q: 'Deep drawing' of sheet metal in the press shop of a workshop consists of:

options.A: Drawing wire out of a rod by pulling it through a die
options.B: Stretching a sheet over a former entirely by hand tools
options.C: Cutting deep grooves in a sheet before it is bent
options.D: Pressing a flat sheet blank with a punch into a die so as to form a hollow, cup-shaped article

e: Deep drawing presses a flat sheet blank with a punch into a die to form a hollow, cup-shaped article without appreciably thinning the sheet. It is a press shop operation, distinct from drawing wire through a die.

q: An irregular-shaped casting has to be held on a lathe for turning, its jaws having to be set one by one to grip it truly. The chuck used for such work is the:

options.A: Three-jaw self-centring chuck
options.B: Four-jaw independent chuck, in which each jaw is adjusted separately
options.C: Magnetic chuck
options.D: Collet chuck

e: An irregular-shaped casting needs a four-jaw independent chuck, in which each jaw is adjusted separately. The jaws can thus be set one by one to grip the casting and bring the required surface true for turning.

q: In forging in the smithy of a workshop, 'drawing down' (drawing out) of a heated bar consists of:

options.A: Hammering it so that its length increases while its cross-section is reduced
options.B: Hammering it so that its cross-section increases while its length is reduced
options.C: Cutting the bar to the length required for the job
options.D: Bending the bar through the angle required for the job

e: Drawing down or drawing out in forging is hammering a heated bar so that its length increases while its cross-section is reduced. It is the opposite of upsetting, where cross-section increases and length reduces.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In up (conventional) milling, the cutter rotates in the same direction as the feed of the work.
2. In down (climb) milling, the cutter rotates in the same direction as the feed of the work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In up or conventional milling the cutter rotates against the direction of feed, so statement 1, which says it rotates in the same direction as feed, is wrong. In down or climb milling the cutter rotates in the same direction as the feed of the work; only statement 2 is correct.

q: 'Chipping', as done by a fitter in a workshop, consists of:

options.A: Breaking up condemned castings into scrap
options.B: Scribing the lines of a job on the surface of the metal
options.C: Removing excess metal from a surface with a cold chisel and hammer
options.D: Cutting internal threads in a hole with a tap

e: Chipping is removing excess metal from a surface with a cold chisel and hammer, as done by a fitter to remove surplus stock, fins or rough projections before filing or machining to finish.

q: A long and slender shaft being turned on a lathe tends to spring away from the cutting tool and to vibrate, spoiling the accuracy of the turning. During such turning, the shaft is supported by means of a:

options.A: Mandrel on which the shaft is mounted
options.B: Face plate bolted to the lathe spindle
options.C: Tool post carrying the cutting tool
options.D: Steady rest fixed to the lathe bed, which supports the shaft at an intermediate point

e: A long slender shaft under turning is supported at an intermediate point by a steady rest fixed to the lathe bed. The steady rest prevents the shaft from springing away from the tool and vibrating, preserving turning accuracy.

q: A V-block is used by a fitter in a workshop for:

options.A: Holding round bars and shafts steadily while they are marked out, drilled or machined
options.B: Measuring the angles of tapered workpieces
options.C: Supporting the bed of a lathe at its ends
options.D: Checking the squareness of two surfaces

e: A V-block has a V-shaped groove that locates round bars and shafts steadily in one position. It is used to hold them while they are marked out, drilled or machined, often with a clamp.

q: A try square is used in fitting work in a workshop for:

options.A: Scribing circles and arcs on a workpiece
options.B: Checking that surfaces and edges are at right angles to each other, and for marking lines at right angles
options.C: Measuring the diameter of shafts and holes
options.D: Testing the hardness of a finished surface

e: A try square is used in fitting work to check that surfaces and edges are at right angles to each other and to mark lines at right angles to an edge, its stock resting against the reference edge and its blade giving the square line.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Value analysis is applied only to products which have already been withdrawn from production.
2. Value engineering applies the same value approach at the design stage itself, before the product goes into manufacture.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Value engineering applies the value approach at the design stage itself, before the product goes into manufacture, so statement 2 is correct. Value analysis is not confined to withdrawn products - it is applied to products in current production to reduce cost without impairing function - so statement 1 is wrong.

q: An outside caliper is used in a fitting shop for:

options.A: Reading the bore of a hole directly off its own scale
options.B: Scribing circles on a workpiece
options.C: Measuring the outside diameter or thickness of a workpiece by setting it on the work and transferring the size to a steel rule
options.D: Measuring the depth of a hole or recess

e: An outside caliper has no scale of its own; its legs are set on the outside diameter or thickness of the work and the size is then transferred to a steel rule for reading, unlike an inside caliper or depth gauge.

q: Thick steel plates welded without any preparation are found to crack along the joint as the weld cools. Such cracking is guarded against in welding practice by:

options.A: Preheating the joint area before welding, so that the weld cools slowly and evenly
options.B: Quenching the welded joint in water immediately after welding
options.C: Completing the weld as fast as possible in a single run
options.D: Leaving a wide gap between the plates at the joint

e: Preheating thick plates before welding slows and evens the cooling of the weld, reducing thermal stresses and hardening that cause cracking on cooling; quenching or fast welding would aggravate the stresses.

q: 'Porosity', as a defect in a welded joint, means:

options.A: A groove melted into the parent metal at the edge of the weld
options.B: Excess weld metal deposited above the surface of the joint
options.C: Lack of fusion between the weld metal and the parent metal
options.D: Small cavities or blow-holes in the weld metal, caused by gases trapped in it as it solidified

e: Porosity is a weld defect consisting of small cavities or blow-holes in the weld metal formed by gases trapped during solidification; a groove at the weld edge is undercut and non-union is lack of fusion.

q: By 'penetration' of a welded joint is meant:

options.A: The length of the weld bead deposited at the joint
options.B: The depth to which the weld metal has fused into the parent metal at the joint
options.C: The width of the weld bead at the surface of the joint
options.D: The quantity of electrode consumed on the joint

e: Penetration is the depth to which the weld metal has fused into the parent metal at the joint; it is measured into the joint, not along the bead length, across its width or by electrode consumption.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In a transition fit, the actual sizes of the hole and the shaft, within their tolerances, may result either in a small clearance or in a small interference when the parts are assembled.
2. A transition fit occupies an intermediate position between a clearance fit and an interference fit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a transition fit lies between clearance and interference fits, and depending on where the actual hole and shaft sizes fall within tolerance, assembly may give a small clearance or a small interference.

q: 'Anodising' of an aluminium article in a workshop consists of:

options.A: Forming a protective oxide film on its surface by making it the anode in an electrolytic bath
options.B: Coating it with zinc by dipping it in molten zinc
options.C: Covering it with a sprayed coat of paint
options.D: Polishing it to a bright finish with an abrasive

e: Anodising forms a protective oxide film on aluminium by making the article the anode in an electrolytic bath; dipping in molten zinc is galvanising, not anodising.

q: 'Stress relieving' heat treatment of a welded or cast component is carried out in order to:

options.A: Harden the surface of the component against wear
options.B: Increase the tensile strength of the component greatly
options.C: Coat the component against rusting in service
options.D: Relieve the internal stresses set up in it during welding, casting or machining, by heating it uniformly and cooling it slowly, without materially changing its structure

e: Stress relieving heats a welded, cast or machined component uniformly and cools it slowly to remove internal stresses without materially changing its structure; it is not a hardening, strengthening or anti-rust treatment.

q: The tread of a railway wheel is given a slight cone (coning of wheels) mainly in order that:

options.A: The weight of the wheel is reduced
options.B: The wheelset tends to keep itself central on a straight track and can negotiate curves, the outer wheel rolling on a larger effective diameter than the inner wheel
options.C: The tyre can be fitted on the wheel centre more easily
options.D: The flange of the wheel is prevented from ever touching the rail

e: Wheel treads are coned so the wheelset self-centres on straight track and, on curves, the outer wheel rolls on a larger effective diameter than the inner wheel, matching the longer outer rail path.

q: 'Chaplets' used in a foundry mould are:

options.A: Small lumps of moulding sand used for patching the mould
options.B: Hand tools used for ramming the sand in the mould
options.C: Small metal supports placed in the mould to hold the core in its correct position while the metal is poured
options.D: Gauges used for checking the size of the mould cavity

e: Chaplets are small metal supports placed in a foundry mould to hold the core in its correct position while molten metal is poured around it.

q: The 'grade' of a grinding wheel refers to:

options.A: The size of the abrasive grains used in the wheel
options.B: The material of the abrasive used in the wheel
options.C: The shape and size of the wheel itself
options.D: The hardness of the wheel, that is, the strength with which the bond holds the abrasive grains in place

e: The grade of a grinding wheel denotes its hardness, that is the strength with which the bond holds the abrasive grains; grain size is called grit and the abrasive material is a separate characteristic.

q: 'Burnishing' of a machined surface in a workshop is a finishing process in which:

options.A: The surface is smoothed and brightened by rubbing it with a hard, smooth tool, the metal being made to flow on the surface without being appreciably removed
options.B: The surface is finished by grinding it with a fine abrasive wheel
options.C: The surface is built up by depositing a layer of another metal
options.D: The surface is cleaned by etching it with acid

e: Burnishing smooths and brightens a surface by rubbing it with a hard smooth tool so the surface metal flows without appreciable removal, unlike grinding, plating or acid etching.

q: Work held between the centres of a lathe is driven round by means of:

options.A: The lead screw of the lathe
options.B: A lathe carrier (dog) clamped to the workpiece, which engages with the driving plate on the spindle
options.C: The tailstock centre of the lathe
options.D: The steady rest fixed to the lathe bed

e: Work held between lathe centres is driven by a lathe carrier or dog clamped to the workpiece, which engages the driving plate on the spindle; the lead screw only provides feed motion.

q: A dividing (indexing) head, as used with a milling machine in a workshop, serves to:

options.A: Divide the production programme of the workshop among its shops
options.B: Hold the milling cutter on the machine spindle
options.C: Rotate the workpiece by exact amounts and hold it indexed, so that equally spaced divisions, such as teeth or flutes, can be milled round it
options.D: Measure the graduations engraved on a steel rule

e: A dividing or indexing head rotates the workpiece by exact amounts and holds it indexed so that equally spaced divisions such as gear teeth or flutes can be milled around it.

q: A 'comparator' used for precision inspection in a workshop is an instrument which:

options.A: Measures the absolute size of a workpiece directly from a scale engraved on it
options.B: Compares two workpieces by weighing them against each other
options.C: Checks the hardness of a workpiece by comparing its colour
options.D: Compares the size of a workpiece with a standard, such as slip gauges, and shows the difference, magnified, on a dial or scale

e: A comparator does not read absolute size directly; it compares the workpiece with a standard such as slip gauges and shows the difference, magnified, on a dial or scale.

q: 'Dowel pins' are used in the assembly of machine parts in a workshop in order to:

options.A: Join two parts permanently, in place of rivets
options.B: Lock nuts on bolts against slackening in service
options.C: Provide a screwed fastening between two parts
options.D: Locate two mating parts accurately in their correct relative position, so that they come together in the same position at every assembly

e: Dowel pins locate two mating parts accurately in their correct relative position so they assemble in the same position every time; they are locating devices, not permanent fasteners or locking devices.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under historical costing, the cost of a job is ascertained only after the expenditure on it has actually been incurred.
2. Historical costing is the method used to quote in advance the price of a one-off job for an outside party.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 alone is correct: under historical costing the job cost is known only after expenditure is actually incurred, so it cannot be used to quote a price in advance for a one-off outside job.

q: Provision for the construction and expansion of railway workshops and production units is made under:

options.A: Plan Head 42 - Workshops and Production Units
options.B: Plan Head 21 - Rolling Stock
options.C: Plan Head 41 - Machinery and Plant
options.D: Plan Head 72 - Manufacturing Suspense

e: Construction and expansion of railway workshops and production units is provided under Plan Head 42 - Workshops and Production Units; Plan Head 21 is Rolling Stock and Plan Head 41 is Machinery and Plant.

q: A manufacture job for an outside party is in progress on a deposit-work basis. Midway through the work, it is found that the deposit recovered in advance will be exhausted by the work still remaining to be done. The correct course is to:

options.A: Continue the work and recover the balance at the time of delivery, in all cases
options.B: Demand a further deposit from the party to cover the expected cost before the work is carried further
options.C: Transfer the balance of the cost to shop on-cost of the shop
options.D: Stop booking further cost to the work order while the work continues

e: On a deposit work, work must not proceed beyond the deposit recovered; when the advance is about to be exhausted, a further deposit covering the expected remaining cost must be demanded before the work is carried further.

q: The tailstock of a centre lathe serves mainly to:

options.A: Support the outer end of long work held between centres, and to hold drills and reamers for work on the end of the job
options.B: House the main spindle and the speed-change mechanism of the lathe
options.C: Carry the cutting tool along the bed of the lathe
options.D: Generate the feed motion for thread cutting

e: The tailstock supports the outer end of long work held between centres and also holds drills and reamers for operations on the end of the job; the headstock houses the main spindle.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In cost control in a workshop, reports to management draw attention mainly to the significant deviations from standard or budget, so that attention is concentrated where it is most needed.
2. Effective cost control requires that every variance, however trivial, be investigated in the same detail.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 alone is correct: cost control by exception concentrates on significant deviations from standard or budget; investigating every trivial variance in equal detail is neither required nor economical.

q: The headstock of a centre lathe is the part which:

options.A: Slides along the bed and carries the saddle of the lathe
options.B: Supports the tail end of the workpiece
options.C: Checks the accuracy of the finished work
options.D: Houses the main spindle, which it carries in its bearings and through which the workpiece is rotated

e: The headstock houses the main spindle, carried in its bearings, through which the workpiece is rotated; the carriage slides on the bed and the tailstock supports the other end of the work.

q: A surface gauge, as used on a surface plate in a fitting shop, is used for:

options.A: Measuring the internal diameter of a bore
options.B: Checking the pitch of a screw thread
options.C: Scribing lines on work at a set height from the datum surface, and for checking heights and parallelism
options.D: Marking the centre of a hole before drilling

e: A surface gauge on a surface plate scribes lines at a set height from the datum surface and is also used for checking heights and parallelism during marking out.

q: At its periodical calibration, a working gauge in a shop is found to be worn beyond the permissible limit. The correct course is to:

options.A: Continue using the gauge till the end of the year
options.B: Correct the cost of every past job by the amount of the error
options.C: Hand the gauge over to another shop where tolerances are looser, without any record
options.D: Withdraw the gauge from use for adjustment or replacement, and have the work measured with it since its last satisfactory check verified again

e: A gauge found worn beyond the permissible limit at calibration must be withdrawn from use for adjustment or replacement, and work measured with it since its last satisfactory check must be verified again.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Variations in a production process which arise from chance (common) causes inherent in the process itself cannot be wholly removed and do not, by themselves, call for stopping the process.
2. Variations arising from assignable causes, shown by points going beyond the control limits, call for investigation and removal of the cause.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: chance or common-cause variation is inherent in a process and does not by itself call for stopping it, while points beyond control limits indicate assignable causes to be investigated and removed.

q: Brittleness of a material means that it:

options.A: Breaks or fractures with little or no deformation when subjected to a load
options.B: Can be drawn out into wires without rupture
options.C: Can be hammered or rolled out into thin sheets without rupture
options.D: Absorbs heavy shock loads without fracture

e: Brittleness is the property of breaking or fracturing with little or no deformation under load; drawability is ductility, hammering into sheets is malleability and shock absorption is toughness.

q: In a foundry, 'shake-out' (knock-out) of a casting means:

options.A: Shaking the moulding box while the sand is being rammed in it
options.B: Shaking the casting in a barrel to clean its surface
options.C: Vibrating the cupola to settle the charge fed into it
options.D: Breaking open the mould after the casting has solidified and cooled, and removing the casting from the sand

e: Shake-out or knock-out is breaking open the mould after the casting has solidified and cooled and removing the casting from the sand.

q: The backing sand used in a foundry mould is:

options.A: The fine sand placed against the pattern, which gives the finish to the casting
options.B: The bulk of the mould behind the facing layer, consisting mainly of old, re-used sand
options.C: The sand sprinkled on the parting surface to prevent the two halves of the mould from sticking together
options.D: The sand used only for making cores for hollow castings

e: Backing sand forms the bulk of the mould behind the facing layer and consists mainly of old re-used sand; the fine sand against the pattern is facing sand.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Maintainability of a machine means the ease and speed with which it can be restored to working order after a failure.
2. Other things being equal, a machine which fails less often and is repaired more quickly will show higher availability for productive work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: maintainability is the ease and speed of restoring a machine after failure, and lower failure frequency combined with quicker repair gives higher availability for productive work.

q: A welded frame comes out warped and out of shape after cooling, although the welds themselves are sound. This warping of the fabricated work is known as:

options.A: Porosity of the weld metal
options.B: Undercut at the edge of the weld
options.C: Lack of penetration of the joint
options.D: Distortion, arising from uneven heating and contraction during welding

e: Warping of a fabricated frame after welding, with sound welds, is distortion caused by uneven heating and contraction during welding; it is distinct from porosity, undercut and lack of penetration.

q: In oxy-acetylene welding, a neutral flame is one in which:

options.A: The two gases burn in a balanced proportion, the flame neither oxidising the metal nor adding carbon to it
options.B: Oxygen is supplied in excess, so that the flame oxidises the metal
options.C: Acetylene is supplied in excess, so that the flame adds carbon to the metal
options.D: No flux is required for welding with it

e: A neutral oxy-acetylene flame burns the gases in balanced proportion so it neither oxidises the metal nor adds carbon to it; excess oxygen gives an oxidising flame and excess acetylene a carburising flame.

q: Bevel gears are used in a machine drive where motion is to be transmitted:

options.A: Between two parallel shafts
options.B: Between two shafts whose axes intersect each other, as at a right angle
options.C: Between a shaft and a rack, to convert rotary motion into straight-line motion
options.D: Only between shafts running at very high speeds

e: Bevel gears transmit motion between two shafts whose axes intersect, commonly at a right angle; parallel shafts use spur or helical gears and a rack converts rotary to straight-line motion.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The cutting speed in a machining operation is the speed at which the cutting edge of the tool moves over the surface of the work.
2. The feed in a machining operation is the distance by which the tool advances into or along the work for each revolution or stroke.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are correct: cutting speed is the speed at which the tool cutting edge moves over the work surface, and feed is the advance of the tool into or along the work per revolution or stroke.

q: The least count of a measuring instrument used in a workshop is:

options.A: The smallest value of measurement that can be read on it accurately
options.B: The largest dimension that the instrument can measure
options.C: The error allowed in the instrument at the time of its manufacture
options.D: The number of divisions marked on its scale

e: The least count of a measuring instrument is the smallest value of measurement that can be read on it accurately.

q: Under selective assembly, as practised for precision fits in a workshop:

options.A: Any component picked at random will assemble correctly with any mating component
options.B: Only the components which fail inspection are assembled together
options.C: Components are assembled together without any measurement
options.D: Components are measured and sorted into groups, and a component is assembled with a mating component of the corresponding group so that the required fit is obtained

e: Under selective assembly, components are measured and sorted into groups and each component is matched with a mating component of the corresponding group so the required fit is obtained despite wider tolerances.

q: In a casting, a weak line or seam is found at the place where two streams of molten metal met in the mould but failed to fuse together properly. This casting defect is known as:

options.A: A shrinkage cavity
options.B: A blow hole
options.C: A cold shut
options.D: A hot tear

e: A cold shut is the weak line or seam formed where two streams of molten metal met in the mould but failed to fuse properly; it differs from shrinkage cavities, blow holes and hot tears.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Roughing cuts in machining remove the bulk of the surplus metal quickly, accuracy and finish not being the main consideration at that stage.
2. Finishing cuts are light cuts taken at the end to bring the work to the exact size and the required surface finish.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: roughing cuts remove the bulk of surplus metal quickly without regard to finish, while finishing cuts are light cuts that bring the work to exact size and required surface finish.

q: A fusible plug fitted in the crown of a boiler furnace in a workshop boiler is a safety device which:

options.A: Blows off steam when the pressure in the boiler exceeds the safe limit
options.B: Melts when the water level falls dangerously low and the plug gets overheated, warning the attendant and preventing damage to the furnace crown
options.C: Indicates the level of water in the boiler
options.D: Feeds water automatically into the boiler

e: A fusible plug in a boiler furnace crown melts when the water level falls dangerously low and the plug overheats, warning the attendant and preventing damage to the furnace crown; pressure relief is the safety valve's job.

q: Caulking of a riveted joint in boiler and tank work consists of:

options.A: Closing the edges of the plates and the rivet heads with a caulking tool so as to make the joint steam- or water-tight
options.B: Drilling out the defective rivets of the joint
options.C: Heating the joint and hammering the plates flat
options.D: Applying a coat of paint over the joint to stop leakage

e: Caulking closes the edges of plates and rivet heads with a caulking tool to make a riveted joint steam- or water-tight.

q: A starter is provided for a direct-current motor in the electrical shop mainly in order to:

options.A: Increase the starting torque of the motor beyond its rated value
options.B: Convert the direct current supply into alternating current
options.C: Limit the heavy current taken by the motor at the moment of starting, until it picks up speed
options.D: Keep the motor running at a constant speed under all loads

e: A starter limits the heavy current a DC motor takes at the moment of starting, until it picks up speed and develops back EMF; without it the starting current would damage the motor and supply.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The pitch of a screw thread is the distance between corresponding points on two adjacent threads, measured parallel to the axis.
2. In a single-start thread, the lead is equal to the pitch, while in a multi-start thread the lead is a multiple of the pitch.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: pitch is the distance between corresponding points on adjacent threads measured parallel to the axis, and lead equals pitch in a single-start thread and is a multiple of pitch in a multi-start thread.

q: Before a set of coach batteries attended to in the electrical shop is returned to service, the specific gravity of the electrolyte in the cells is measured with a hydrometer and found to be uniformly low. This indicates that:

options.A: The cells are in a discharged condition and require charging before use
options.B: The cells are fully charged and fit for service
options.C: The electrolyte is too strong and must be diluted at once
options.D: The battery has developed a short circuit in every cell

e: Uniformly low specific gravity of battery electrolyte, measured by hydrometer, indicates the cells are discharged and require charging before the coach battery set is returned to service.

q: In the limits and fits system, the deviation of a dimension means:

options.A: The difference between the maximum and minimum limits of the size
options.B: The intentional difference provided between the sizes of the mating hole and shaft
options.C: The wear allowed on a gauge in service
options.D: The difference between a limit of the size (or the actual size) and the basic size from which the limits are reckoned

e: In limits and fits, deviation is the difference between a limit of size, or the actual size, and the basic size; the difference between maximum and minimum limits is the tolerance.

q: A Morse taper, as used on the shanks of drills and on lathe centres in a workshop, is:

options.A: The taper provided on a foundry pattern to allow its withdrawal from the mould
options.B: A standard self-holding taper by which the tool or centre is held firmly in the spindle or tailstock socket by friction, and released when required
options.C: The taper of the point of a centre punch
options.D: The taper provided on the thread of a tapered bolt

e: A Morse taper is a standard self-holding taper on drill shanks and lathe centres, held firmly in the spindle or tailstock socket by friction and released when required.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A job description is a written statement of the duties, responsibilities and working conditions of a job, drawn up from job analysis.
2. A job specification sets out the qualifications, experience and qualities required of the worker who is to hold that job.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a job description states the duties, responsibilities and working conditions of a job from job analysis, while a job specification states the qualifications, experience and qualities required of the job holder.

q: A Pareto analysis of the rejections in a workshop over a period shows that a small number of causes account for the bulk of the rejected work. The use of such an analysis in quality control is that:

options.A: All causes of rejection can be eliminated simultaneously
options.B: The cost of inspection can be charged to the causes of rejection
options.C: Attention and remedial action can be directed first to the few vital causes which produce most of the rejections
options.D: Rejected work can be accepted without rectification

e: Pareto analysis directs attention and remedial action first to the few vital causes that produce most of the rejections, instead of spreading effort over all causes equally.

q: A histogram prepared from the measurements of a component produced in a shop shows:

options.A: The sequence in which the components were produced, hour by hour
options.B: The distribution of the measured values - how they are spread out and where they are centred
options.C: The control limits fixed for the process by the inspector
options.D: The proportion of components to be drawn as a sample for inspection

e: A histogram shows the distribution of measured values - how they are spread out and where they are centred; it does not show production sequence or control limits.

q: A shop loses a large number of its experienced fitters during a year and replaces them with fresh recruits. Although wage rates are unchanged, the unit cost of its outturn rises. This rise is mainly attributable to:

options.A: The cost of recruiting and training the new men, and their lower efficiency and greater spoilage until they pick up the work
options.B: The higher wages payable to fresh recruits
options.C: The increase in the general on-cost rates of the workshop
options.D: The reduction in the allowed times of the jobs of the shop

e: Replacing experienced fitters with fresh recruits raises unit cost through recruitment and training cost and the recruits' lower efficiency and greater spoilage until they pick up the work, even though wage rates are unchanged.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In an open belt drive, the two pulleys rotate in the same direction.
2. In a crossed belt drive, the two pulleys rotate in opposite directions.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: in an open belt drive both pulleys rotate in the same direction, while in a crossed belt drive they rotate in opposite directions.

q: A worm and worm wheel drive is used in workshop machines where:

options.A: The driven shaft must rotate faster than the driving shaft
options.B: Motion is to be transmitted between two shafts which are far apart
options.C: The direction of rotation has to be reversed frequently
options.D: A very large reduction of speed in a single stage of drive is required

e: A worm and worm wheel drive is used where a very large speed reduction in a single stage is required; it reduces speed rather than increasing it.

q: A key, as used in the assembly of a pulley or gear on a shaft in a workshop, is a machine element which:

options.A: Prevents the shaft from bending under load
options.B: Locks the nut fitted on the end of the shaft
options.C: Fits into the keyways of the shaft and the hub and transmits the turning force (torque) from the one to the other
options.D: Couples two lengths of shaft permanently end to end

e: A key fits into the keyways of the shaft and the hub and transmits torque between them, so the pulley or gear rotates with the shaft.
